subject: DPA clarifications — data handling, retention, and subprocessors
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-05T15:20:00-08:00
Subject: DPA clarifications — data handling, retention, and subprocessors

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap of the items you asked us to confirm and next steps so everyone is aligned: 

1) Controller vs processor: Redwood operates as a processor for the inference API. Customers (Acme Payments) are controllers for the data they send to the service. We can include specific language reflecting that role in the DPA redline.

2) Subprocessors: We use a small set of cloud and monitoring subprocessors. I attached the current subprocessor list (see Subprocessor_List_20261205.csv). If you have a required subprocessors review process, we can walk through it.

3) PII & data retention: By default, we retain request/response logs for 30 days for troubleshooting and billing. We offer configurable retention windows down to 0 days for logs and provide options for customer-managed retention for dedicated/private deployments.

4) Logging controls & access: Access to logs is restricted to SRE and support on a least-privilege basis and is auditable. We can add required role-based access descriptions and mention KMS integration for encryption at rest.

5) Data residency: Hosted region choices include US and EU. For EU residency, we can route inference and store logs in the EU region; for additional controls we recommend Private (VPC) deployment.

Next steps: I’m attaching a redline of our standard DPA with clarifications on controller/processor roles and breach notice timelines. Can you confirm whether your legal team needs us to accept a specific breach-notification window (e.g., 72 hours) or if the standard 30-day notification plus good-faith updates is okay?

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Redline_20261205.pdf, Subprocessor_List_20261205.csv

I’ll loop Marissa from legal on the next message for any contract-level questions.

Cheers,
Ben
Ben Carter | Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

- Subprocessors: Please confirm whether any subprocessors have access to full request/response payloads, or if access is restricted to metadata/metrics only. We saw monitoring vendors listed on the screen share and need to know scope of access.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme-payments.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@acme-payments.com>
Date: 2026-12-07T10:35:00-08:00
Subject: Re: DPA clarifications — data handling, retention, and subprocessors

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks for the questions, and great to e-meet you. Quick answers below and next steps: 

1) Controller/Processor clause: Yes — we will add explicit language in the DPA confirming Redwood is a processor and Acme is the controller, and include standard processing instructions referencing permitted processing activities (hosting, storing, processing inference requests, telemetry for service reliability).

2) Subprocessors & access scope: Our subprocessors break down into (a) cloud infrastructure providers (IaaS) who have no visibility into decrypted payloads when customer-managed keys are used, (b) monitoring/logging vendors who may receive redacted telemetry/metrics by default, and (c) optional analytics partners used only with explicit customer opt-in. None of our listed monitoring vendors have default access to full request/response payloads for hosted customers. For customers requiring zero-access, we recommend Private deployment or Customer-Managed Keys (CMK) so payloads are not exposed to Redwood-operated subprocessors.

3) Breach notification: We understand Acme's preference for a 72-hour initial notice. Our policy is to provide an initial notification within 72 hours for confirmed incidents that materially affect customer data. We will include a 72-hour initial notification clause in the DPA redline and commit to timely updates thereafter (we'll also describe remediation and post-incident reporting timelines).

4) Retention & logging controls: We will accept contract language to allow for configurable retention windows and will include options for log minimization and access auditing. For hosted customers we can offer a 30-day default with the ability to shorten upon request; for Dedicated/Private we can support custom retention per the deployment agreement.

Next steps: 
- I attached a redline with the explicit controller/processor clause, the 72-hour initial breach notice clause, and an annotated subprocessor access statement. Please review and let us know any redline you'd like to propose.
- If your counsel wants to discuss, I can join a 30-minute call tomorrow at 2pm ET — let me know if that works.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Redline_20261205.pdf, Subprocessor_List_20261205.csv

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Legal — Redwood Inference
